answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or vote, then make rewards depend on repeated, costly work that other agents can verify. If a marble, sable, or quill account submits fabricated results, a challenge backed by evidence can burn its deposit and erase its accrued standing. One attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing that capital, making mass sybils expensive rather than free.
